patients.label: Index woman with post-RYGB severe malnutrition

fields.index_subject_description: 55-year-old woman with severe malnutrition after RYGB despite reported nutritional adherence
fields.care_setting: Initial center assessment, inpatient nutrition and revisional surgery; prior RYGB at private hospital

evidence.quote: A 55-year-old businesswoman, with a medical history of obesity, arterial hypertension, and insulin resistance, and a surgical history of three cesarean sections and a fundoplication performed 17 years ago, underwent RYGB at a private hospital. At the time of bariatric surgery, her weight was 107 kg, height 1.60 m, and BMI 41.7 kg/m². One year and nine months after surgery, the patient consulted our center for the first time, reporting generalized weakness, asthenia, and adynamia, despite adherence to supplementation and nutritional recommendations, as she described. A complete assessment and laboratory workup revealed normocytic normochromic anemia and severe malnutrition (albumin: 2.5 g/dL).
She was hospitalized for mixed (enteral/parenteral) nutrition and evaluation for revisional surgery.

facts.clinical_statement: Index woman presented with weakness and malnutrition after RYGB

summary.text: A 55-year-old woman with prior obesity, hypertension, insulin resistance, three cesarean sections and remote fundoplication underwent RYGB at 107 kg/BMI 41.7. One year nine months later she presented with weakness, asthenia and adynamia despite self-reported nutritional adherence. Workup found normocytic normochromic anemia and severe malnutrition; initial albumin 2.5 in prose conflicts 2.8 in Table 1. Psychiatric/psychological disorders were ruled out and upper-GI endoscopy showed normal esophagus/candy-cane limb, 5 cm pouch and 2 cm anastomosis without pathology.

Symptoms worsened after conservative nutrition was selected, with weight 66.9 kg/BMI 26 and severe nutritional laboratory abnormalities. One month of mixed enteral/parenteral support improved nutrition before revision. Laparoscopy found adhesions and otherwise RYGB anatomy; limb measurements led authors to suspect hyper-response rather than an anatomical malnutrition cause. A 3 cm gastro-gastric anastomosis was constructed with a Tri-Staple cartridge and closed in two layers with Monocryl 2-0. Methylene-blue testing showed no leak; surgery lasted 150 minutes with estimated 50 mL blood loss.

Recovery was uneventful. Postoperative day-one water-soluble contrast showed passage through alimentary limb/native stomach/duodenum without leaks. Discharge followed with nutritional recommendations, but the exact following-day anchor is uncertain. Post-surgical Table 1 labs have an unspecified draw time. At three months symptoms resolved, weight 72 kg/BMI 28 and author-reported labs normalized; at five months she remained symptom-free with optimal nutrition and normal labs. Generic 6–12 month monitoring advice is background, not an index completed plan.
